filled_trades.rationale: Apple Q4 beat: revenue $94.9B vs $94.3B est, Services record $24.97B, Apple Intelligence adoption strong. High conviction buy ahead of holiday iPhone 16 cycle.
Amazon Q3 beat: AWS $27.5B (+19% YoY) and record operating income $17.4B. Multi-year AI infrastructure demand tailwind. Position sized at 2.3% of portfolio.
Microsoft Azure acceleration to 33% growth, Copilot 300M seats. Adding to existing position on strong Q1 FY2025 results.

research_reports.summary: Apple Q4 FY2024 beat on revenue ($94.9B vs $94.3B est.) and EPS ($1.64 vs $1.60 est.). Services reached a record $24.97B. Apple Intelligence iOS 18.1 rollout showing strong adoption. iPhone 16 holiday demand supported by supply chain checks indicating 10% production order increase.
citations: [1] (2024-10-31 via Reuters): Apple Inc. reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2024 revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year-over-year, beating analyst consensus of $94.3 billion. EPS of $1.64 beat the $1.60 estimate.
[2] (2024-10-29 via Bloomberg): Apple began rolling out its Apple Intelligence AI features with iOS 18.1. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate 20% of iPhone users upgraded within the first week.
[3] (2024-10-22 via Barclays Research): Supply chain checks suggest Apple has increased iPhone 16 Pro production orders by 10% for Q4.

research_reports.summary: Microsoft Q1 FY2025 revenue $65.6B (+16% YoY). Azure accelerated to 33% growth, beating 29% prior quarter. Copilot enterprise seats at 300M. CFO guided Q2 Azure 34-35% growth — acceleration continues.
citations: [1] (2024-10-30 via CNBC): Microsoft reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $65.6 billion, up 16% YoY. Azure cloud revenue grew 33% YoY, accelerating from 29% the prior quarter.
[2] (2024-10-24 via Goldman Sachs): Microsoft disclosed that Copilot for Microsoft 365 now has over 300 million paid seats eligible for the $30/month add-on.

research_reports.summary: Alphabet Q3 beat on all metrics. Search +12%, Cloud +35%. AI Overviews showing higher monetization than traditional search. Gemini integration progressing. Strong FCF generation. Position held — no new action.

[2] (2024-10-30 via Deutsche Bank): Alphabet CFO noted AI Overviews in Search showing higher monetization rates than traditional search results.

research_reports.summary: Amazon Q3 beat: AWS $27.5B (+19%), record operating income $17.4B with 38.1% margins. Trainium2 chip launched. Multi-year AI infrastructure backlog building. Adding on strong fundamentals.

research_reports.summary: Blackwell GPU shipments confirmed, demand exceeds supply with 12-month backlog. Data center Q3 revenue tracking ~$30B. Supply constraints from TSMC CoWoS packaging are a near-term risk. Holding existing exposure — not adding at current valuation.
citations: [1] (2024-10-28 via Bank of America): Nvidia confirmed Blackwell GPU shipments began in Q3 FY2025. CEO Jensen Huang noted demand far exceeds supply with a 12-month backlog.
[2] (2024-10-21 via Needham): Taiwan Semiconductor flagged capacity constraints for CoWoS advanced packaging. Some analysts warn supply limitations could push Q4 guidance below street expectations.

narrative:
Trading Day Summary — October 31, 2024

A strong earnings day for our core holdings. Apple and Amazon both reported Q3/Q4 beats after market close on October 31, with Apple's Services revenue reaching a record $24.97B and Amazon's AWS posting 19% growth at $27.5B.

We initiated positions in AAPL (200 shares, $45,792 notional) and AMZN (120 shares, $23,187 notional) on the earnings catalysts, and added to our MSFT position (50 shares, $21,430 notional) on continued Azure acceleration to 33% YoY growth.

All three trades exceeded the $20,000 HITL threshold. The Risk Committee reviewed and approved all trades, noting that combined tech sector concentration reached 52% — within our 60% soft limit but warranting monitoring.

End-of-day portfolio value: $999,771.85 vs starting value of $1,000,000.00 (-0.02% daily return).
S&P 500 (SPY) returned +0.48% on the day. Portfolio alpha: -0.51%.

Risk note: Tech sector concentration elevated. NVDA held — supply constraint risk acknowledged. No further additions to Nvidia without new evidence on Blackwell yield rates.
